Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:10:1.hebrew: מתניתין נמי דיקא - כרב חסדא, דגינה אינו בונה במועד כדרכו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:10:1.english: The Mishnah is also precise - Like Rav Chisda, that [the wall of] a garden one does not build on the festival in his [usual] manner.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:11:1.hebrew: אלא לאו בגינה - ובשביעית בונה כדרכו, אבל במועד אינו בונה כדרכו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:11:1.english: Rather, is it not in a garden? - And during the Sabbatical Year he builds in his usual manner, whereas during the [intermediate days of the] Festival he does not build in his usual manner.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:12:1.english: They examine the leprous marks to be lenient - That is to say, the priest examines a mark of leprosy on the Festival to declare [him] pure.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:12:2.hebrew: לא להחמיר - שאם רואה הכהן שהוא טמא, אינו אומר כלום; שאם מטמאו, נמצא מצערו במועד, ורחמנא אמר (דברים טז) ושמחת בחגך:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:12:2.english: Not to be stringent - For if the priest sees that he is [ritually] impure, he says nothing; for if he declares him impure, he ends up causing him distress on the Festival, and the Merciful One said (Deuteronomy 16[:14]): "And you shall rejoice on your festival."

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:13:1.hebrew: שאם אתה נזקק לו להקל, אתה נזקק לו להחמיר - כלומר, מאחר שרואהו הכהן, אומר בין הוא טמא בין הוא טהור:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:13:1.english: For if you attend to him to be lenient, you [must] attend to him to be stringent - That is to say, once the priest examines him, he states whether he is impure or whether he is pure.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:14:1.hebrew: א"ר נראין לי דברי ר' מאיר במוסגר - שרואין, ודברי רבי יוסי במוחלט:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:14:1.english: Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] said: The statement of Rabbi Meir appears [correct] to me with regard to a quarantined [leper] - That they examine [the symptoms], and the statement of Rabbi Yosei [appears correct] with regard to a confirmed [leper].

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:15:1.hebrew: בהסגר ראשון - שאם מטהר ליה, משמח ליה; אי לא מטהר ליה, לא מטמא ליה יותר מדמעיקרא, אלא מסגר ליה פעם שניה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:15:1.english: With regard to [one in his] first quarantine - For if [the priest] declares him pure, he makes him rejoice; if he does not declare him pure, he does not render him more impure than [he was] originally, rather he quarantines him a second time.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:1:1.hebrew: עד כמה - מרוחקין הני תרי חורי נמלים, דכי איכא נהרא בינייהו וליכא גישרא, דאין מכירין הני בחורי דהני:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:1:1.english: Up to what [distance] - are these two ant holes distanced [from each other], such that when there is a river between them and there is no bridge, these [ants] do not recognize the holes of those [ants].

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:1:2.hebrew: עד פרסה - אי ליכא פרסה בינייהו, אע"ג דאיכא נהרא וליכא מעבר, מכירין הני בחורי דהני:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:1:2.english: Up to a parasang - If there is not a parasang between them, even though there is a river and there is no crossing, these [ants] recognize the holes of those [ants].

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:2:1.hebrew: נועץ שפוד - במקום שהן מצוין, ומרדה האדמה וממעך אותן:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:2:1.english: He inserts a spit - In a place where they are found, and removes the earth and crushes them.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:4:2.hebrew: דפנא - בייר. וקעבד גדר מדפנא, ומגדל אותה מהוצי הדקל:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:4:2.english: Dafna - Baier [Old French for bay tree]. And he makes a fence of bay [branches], and weaves it with palm fronds.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:5:1.english: One fills [it] with stone - He places stones one on top of another.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:5:2.hebrew: אמר רב חסדא לא שנו - דאמר מתני' מקרין, אבל אינו בונה כדרכו:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:5:2.english: Rav Ḥisda said: They taught [this] only - that the Mishnah says one seals [the breach], but he does not build in his [usual] manner.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:5:3.english: In [the case of] a garden wall - For there is no excessive loss if people enter it.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:5:4.english: However, with a courtyard wall, he builds in his usual manner - For there is greater loss if thieves enter it and steal his property.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:6:2.hebrew: סותר ובונה כדרכו - דהיינו כותל חצר, מסייע ליה לרב חסדא:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:6:2.english: One may demolish and rebuild [it] in his [usual] manner - That is, a courtyard wall, [and thus it] supports Rav Ḥisda.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:6:3.english: Due to the danger - So that it does not fall on those walking in the public domain.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:7:1.hebrew: שלא מפני הסכנה לא - קשיא לרב חסדא, דאמר בכותל חצר בונה כדרכו, אע"פ דליכא סכנה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:7:1.english: Not due to the danger, no - [This is] a difficulty for Rav Chisda, who said regarding a courtyard wall [that] one may build in his [usual] manner even though there is no danger.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:8:1.hebrew: תריץ - לא קשיא לרב חסדא, דהא דקתני במקום סכנה, היינו דסתר לה כשגוחה, ובונה לה שפיר:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:8:1.english: [He] resolves [it] - [It is] not a difficulty for Rav Chisda, for that which [the baraita] teaches "in a case of danger," that is [to say] that he demolishes it when it is leaning, and builds it properly.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:8:2.hebrew: הכא - דקאמר רב חסדא שלא במקום סכנה, בונה כדרכה כשהיא סתורה קודם לכן, אבל לא סתר לה במועד:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:8:2.english: Here - [regarding] which Rav Chisda said, [where it is] not a place of danger, one builds [the wall] in its usual manner when it was [already] demolished beforehand, but one may not demolish it during the festival.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:9:1.hebrew: התם - במקום סכנה, לסתור משום דאיכא סכנה, ולא ליבני, דבבנין ליכא סכנה:
Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:9:1.english: There - In a place of danger, [let him] demolish because there is danger, and not rebuild, for in rebuilding there is no danger.

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:9:2.english: If so - [meaning] that he does not rebuild [it].

Rashi on Moed Katan 7a:9:3.english: They would refrain and not demolish - and there would be danger.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 7a:10:1.hebrew: אמר רב אשי מתניתין נמי דיקא - פסק בתוס' דהר"ר פרץ דהלכתא הכי, דכותל חצר מותר לבנותו; ופירש דהיינו דוקא במקום סמוך לרה"ר שיש לו לחוש לגנבים, אבל בין חצר לחצר ומשום בני חצר, אסור לבנותו כדרכו:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 7a:10:1.english: Rav Ashi said: The Mishnah is also precise - In the Tosafot of HaRav Rabbi Peretz it is ruled that the halakha is thus, that it is permitted to build a courtyard wall; and he explained that this [applies] specifically in a place adjacent to the public domain, where one must be concerned about thieves, but between one courtyard and another, and [where the concern is] on account of the residents of the courtyard, it is forbidden to build it in its usual manner.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 7a:14:1.hebrew: אמר רבי נראין דברי ר"מ במוסגר - מה שפירש בקונטרס דמוסגר אסור בתשמיש המטה, לא נדע מנין לו; דהא תנן בפרק קמא דמגילה (דף ח:): "אין בין מוסגר למוחלט אלא פריעה ופרימה", משמע דלענין תשמיש המטה שוין: דלמאן דאמר מוחלט מותר, כל שכן דמוסגר מותר; ולמ"ד דמוחלט אסור, ה"ה מוסגר אסור. דהא מוחלט מאי טעמא דאסור? משום דאיכא ק"ו לימי חלוטו, כדאמרינן בשמעתין; והכי נמי ק"ו לימי הסגירו, וגמרינן ימי הסגר מימי ספרו. ואי משום דאין טעון פריעה ופרימה — בימי ספרו נמי אין טעון פריעה ופרימה. והא דקאמר התם בגמרא: "הא לענין שילוח טומאה זה וזה שוין", ה"ה לענין תשמיש המטה הן שוין, אלא לא פסיק ליה לאיסור או להיתר. וגם מה שפירש בקונט' דמוסגר אינו משתלח חוץ לג' מחנות — מזה חזר בו, דהא בפרק קמא דמגילה (דף ח:) קאמר: "הא לענין שילוח זה וזה שוין". ולפי זה קשה: מאי שייך צוותא דאשתו וצוותא דעלמא במוסגר ובמוחלט? בשלמא צוותא דעלמא יש ליישב, שהוא צריך פריעה ופרימה כשהוא מוחלט, ו"טמא טמא יקרא", ופורש מבני אדם בימי חלוטו יותר מבימי הסגירו; אבל לתשמיש שניהן שוין! ע"כ נראה דהא דקאמר "מר סבר צוותא דעלמא ניחא ליה, ומר סבר צוותא דאשתו עדיף" — אמוחלט קאי. וה"פ: נראין דברי ר' מאיר במוחלט דרואין, דאי מטמא ליה — תחילה נמי טמא הוה, ואי מטהר ליה — מאי אפסדיה? דצוותא דאשתו אינו חושש, דצוותא דעלמא עדיפא ליה. ונראין דברי ר' יוסי במוסגר, דמטמא ליה ופסיד צוותא דעלמא, שיהיה טעון פריעה ופרימה ו"טמא טמא יקרא" וצריך לפרוש מבני אדם, וגם יפסיד שיצטער שעד עתה היה מצפה להיות טהור, ואין מצפה עתה ליטהר. ותנא אחרינא סבר צוותא דאשתו ניחא ליה, והכי פירושו: נראין דברי ר' מאיר דרואין במוסגר, דאי מטמא ליה לא יפסיד, דשניהן — מוסגר ומוחלט — דינם שוה חוץ מפריעה ופרימה; ובהך הפסד אינו חושש, אפי' קרינא ליה הפסד צוותא דעלמא כדפי', אינו חושש אלא אצוותא דאשתו. אבל מוחלט אין רואין, דאי מטהר ליה יפסיד צוותא דאשתו, דקסבר צוותא דאשתו עדיפא ליה מצוותא דעלמא. וקצת ק"ל: מהו "נראין דברי ר"מ"? הא לית ליה לרבי מאיר כלל דהכהן מחויב לומר, ואי בעי שתיק; ור' קסבר דלעולם כהן אינו רשאי לשתוק כלל, ולדברי ר' לא תמצא בשום אחד "רואין להקל ולא להחמיר", דאינו רשאי לשתוק כלל, והכי הוה ליה למימר: "נראין דברי ר' יוסי כו', ואין נראין דברי יוסי כו'". והכי איתא בשמעתין דטיפת חלב (חולין דף קט.):
Tosafot on Moed Katan 7a:14:1.english: Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] said: The words of Rabbi Meir appear [correct] regarding a quarantined [leper] - [Regarding] that which Rashi explained, that a quarantined [leper] is forbidden from marital relations, we do not know from where he [derived] this; for we learned in a Mishnah in the first chapter of Megillah (8b): "There is no [difference] between a quarantined [leper] and a confirmed [leper] except [the obligations of] letting the hair grow wild and rending [the garments]," which implies that with respect to marital relations they are equal. For according to the one who says a confirmed [leper] is permitted [marital relations], all the more so is a quarantined [leper] permitted; and according to the one who says that a confirmed [leper] is forbidden, the same law applies that a quarantined [leper] is forbidden. For what is the reason that a confirmed [leper] is forbidden? Because there is an a fortiori argument [applying] to the days of his confirmation, as we say in our sugya; and so too, there is an a fortiori argument for the days of his quarantine, and we derive the days of quarantine from the days of his counting. And if [you object] because he is not required [to observe] letting the hair grow wild and rending [the garments during quarantine] — during the days of his counting too, he is not required [to observe] letting the hair grow wild and rending [the garments]. And [as for] that which [the Gemara] says there: "However, with respect to sending [them] out [and] ritual impurity, both this one and that one are equal," the same law applies that with respect to marital relations they are equal, except that [the Gemara] could not state it definitively as a prohibition or as a permissibility. And also, [regarding] that which Rashi explained, that a quarantined [leper] is not sent out beyond the three camps — from this he retracted, for in the first chapter of Megillah (8b) it says: "However, with respect to sending out, both this one and that one are equal." And according to this, it is difficult: How are "the companionship of his wife" and "the companionship of the general public" relevant to [the distinction between] a quarantined [leper] and a confirmed [leper]? Granted, "the companionship of the general public" can be reconciled, for he requires letting the hair grow wild and rending [the garments] when he is confirmed, and [must call out], "Impure! Impure!" and he separates from people during the days of his confirmation more than during the days of his quarantine; however, with respect to marital relations, both are equal! Therefore, it appears that that which [the Gemara] says, "One Sage holds the companionship of the general public is preferable to him, and one Sage holds the companionship of his wife is preferable" — refers to a confirmed [leper]. And this is its explanation: The words of Rabbi Meir appear [correct] regarding a confirmed [leper], that we examine [him], for if [the priest] declares him impure — previously too he was impure, and if he declares him pure — what has he caused him to lose? For he is not concerned about the companionship of his wife, since the companionship of the general public is preferable to him. And the words of Rabbi Yosei appear [correct] regarding a quarantined [leper], for [the priest] might declare him impure and he will lose the companionship of the general public, since he will be required [to observe] letting the hair grow wild and rending [the garments], and [to call out] "Impure! Impure!" and will need to separate from people, and he will also lose out in that he will be distressed, for until now he was hoping to become pure, whereas now he does not hope to become pure. And the other Tanna holds that the companionship of his wife is preferable to him, and this is its explanation: The words of Rabbi Meir appear [correct] that we examine a quarantined [leper], for if [the priest] declares him impure, he will not lose out, since both of them — a quarantined [leper] and a confirmed [leper] — have the same law except for letting the hair grow wild and rending [the garments]; and about that loss he is not concerned — even if we call it a loss of the companionship of the general public, as I explained, he is only concerned about the companionship of his wife. However, a confirmed [leper] we do not examine, for if [the priest] declares him pure, he will lose the companionship of his wife, as [this Tanna] holds that the companionship of his wife is preferable to him over the companionship of the general public. And it is somewhat difficult for us: What is [the meaning of] "The words of Rabbi Meir appear [correct]"? Surely Rabbi Meir does not hold at all that the priest is obligated to speak, and if he wishes he may remain silent; whereas Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] holds that a priest is never permitted to remain silent at all, and according to the words of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], you will never find in any case "we examine to be lenient and not to be stringent," since he is not permitted to remain silent at all! Rather, this is what he should have said: "The words of Rabbi Yosei appear [correct], etc., and the words of [Rabbi] Yosei do not appear [correct], etc." And so it is in the sugya of a drop of milk (Chullin 109a).

Tosafot on Moed Katan 7a:15:1.hebrew: בהסגר ראשון כולי עלמא לא פליגי - מה שפירש בקונטרס בסוף הסגר ראשון, ומשום הכי רואין: אי טהור — שפיר, ואי עומד בעיניו — תחילה נמי בבית הכלא היה עומד. וקשה: דלמא פשה הנגע ויהיה טמא מוחלט! והכי משמע בנגעים פ"א: דארבע מראות הללו מצטרפין זה עם זה לפטור את העומד סוף שבוע שני, להחליט את שנולד בו מחיה או שער לבן בתחילה, בסוף שבוע ראשון, או בסוף שני לאחר הפטור, להחליט את שנולד בו פיסיון בסוף שבוע ראשון או בסוף שבוע שני. ויש לפרש: "בהסגר ראשון כ"ע לא פליגי דחזי ליה" — הוי הטעם משום ד"לטהרו או לטמאו" לא שייך למדרש עד שעה שצריך לטמאותו, דהיינו בסוף הסגר שני; אבל בסוף הסגר ראשון ראוי הוא להסגיר עוד, ולא יטמאנו. וכל זה דוחק. לכך נראה דברי רבינו יצחק: "בהסגר ראשון" היינו תחילת הסגר ראשון, שיכול לשמח בהן, דהא לא שייך "לטהרו או לטמאו". "בהסגר שני" — והוא בתחילת הסגר שני, שמא אינו יכול לשתוק, והוא הדין בסוף הסגר שני:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 7a:15:1.english: "With regard to the first quarantine, everyone agrees" - Regarding that which Rashi explained, [that this refers to] the end of the first quarantine, and for that reason they examine [him]: if he is pure — well and good, and if it remains as it was — initially too he was standing in confinement [i.e., quarantined]. But this is difficult: perhaps the affliction spread, and he will become a confirmed impure person! And so it is implied in Negaim, Chapter 1: These four appearances combine with one another to exempt that which remains unchanged at the end of the second week; to confirm [as impure] that in which healthy flesh or white hair developed [whether] at the beginning, at the end of the first week, or at the end of the second [week] after exemption; [and] to confirm [as impure] that in which spreading developed at the end of the first week or at the end of the second week. One can explain [Rashi's view]: "With regard to the first quarantine, everyone agrees that he examines him" — the reason is that [the verse] "to pronounce it pure or to pronounce it impure" is not applicable to expound until the time when one needs to pronounce him impure [with confirmed leprosy], which is at the end of the second quarantine; whereas at the end of the first quarantine, he is fit to be quarantined further, and [the priest] will not pronounce him impure. But all of this is forced. Therefore, the words of Rabbeinu Yitzchak appear [correct]: "With regard to the first quarantine" refers to the beginning of the first quarantine, for he can gladden [him] with them, as [the verse] "to pronounce it pure or to pronounce it impure" does not apply. "With regard to the second quarantine" — and this refers to the beginning of the second quarantine, [for] perhaps [the priest] cannot remain silent, and the same applies at the end of the second quarantine.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 7a:1:1.hebrew: עד כמה עד פרסה - דאין מכירין זה את זה ביותר מפרסה, אפי' בלא נהר. א"נ ה"פ: כשיש נהר, מתי קרויין מכירין? עד פרסה, אבל ביותר מיקרי אין מכירין; ודוקא דאיכא נהר:
Tosafot on Moed Katan 7a:1:1.english: Up to what [distance]? Up to a parasang - For [the ants] do not recognize one another at [a distance of] more than a parasang, even without a river. Alternatively, this is its explanation: When there is a river, when are they called "recognizing [one another]"? Up to a parasang, but at more [than a parasang] they are called "not recognizing [one another]," and specifically when there is a river.

Tosafot on Moed Katan 7a:3:1.hebrew: תניא ר"ש בן אלעזר אומר - לא ידענא מה הוא: אם הוא תנא שלישי, או שמא מילתיה דת"ק מפרש, או שמא י"ל דרבי יהודה מודה בשדה לבן הסמוכה לשדה האילן, וחכמים מיירי בשדה הסמוכה לבית השלחין, לא בשדה הסמוכה לבית האילן. ונראה לי דגרסינן הכי: "באיזה שדה לבן מתירין חכמים". ויש ספרים שכתוב בהן: "כשאמרו בשדה לבן שלא כדרכו לא אמרו אלא בשדה לבן הסמוכה לעיר", וקאי על דברי רבי יהודה כו':
Tosafot on Moed Katan 7a:3:1.english: It is taught [in a baraita]: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says - I do not know what his [position] is: whether he is a third Tanna [who disagrees with both the Sages and Rabbi Yehuda], or perhaps he is explaining the statement of the Tanna Kamma, or perhaps one can say that Rabbi Yehuda concedes with regard to a field of grain adjacent to an orchard [that one may trap in his usual manner], whereas the Sages are referring to a field adjacent to an irrigated field, not [only] to a field adjacent to an orchard. And it appears to me that we should read [the text] as follows: "In which field of grain do the Sages permit [trapping in the usual manner]?" And there are texts in which it is written: "When they said, in a field of grain not in his usual manner, they said [it] only regarding a field of grain adjacent to the city," and this refers to the statement of Rabbi Yehuda, etc.
